passages.text: Jesus went on from there and came to His hometown, accompanied by His disciples.
passages.sermon: Jesus left that place.\r\nHe went to His hometown.\r\nHis disciples followed Him.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν καὶ ἔρχεται εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθοῦσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: When the Sabbath came, He began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard Him were astonished. “Where did this man get these ideas?” they asked. “What is this wisdom He has been given? And how can He perform such miracles?
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a teacher and miracle worker.
He came to His hometown with His disciples.
The Sabbath day arrived.
Jesus began to teach in the synagogue.
Many people listened to Him.
They were astonished.
They said, “Where did this man get these things?”
They asked, “What is this wisdom given to Him?”
They also asked, “How are such miracles done by His hands?”
passages.original: καὶ γενομένου σαββάτου ἤρξατο διδάσκειν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ καὶ οἱ πολλοὶ ἀκούοντες ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες Πόθεν τούτῳ ταῦτα καὶ τίς ἡ σοφία ἡ δοθεῖσα τούτῳ καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις τοιαῦται διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ γινόμεναι

passages.text: Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Aren’t His sisters here with us as well?” And they took offense at Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a carpenter.
He was the son of Mary.
He was the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon.
His sisters were also present among the people.
The people took offense at Jesus.
passages.original: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τέκτων ὁ υἱὸς τῆς Μαρίας καὶ ἀδελφὸς Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωσῆτος καὶ Ἰούδα καὶ Σίμωνος καὶ οὐκ εἰσὶν αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ ὧδε πρὸς ἡμᾶς καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ

passages.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Only in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household is a prophet without honor.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people in the synagogue.
Jesus said, “A prophet receives honor everywhere except in his own hometown.
A prophet receives no honor among his own relatives.
A prophet receives no honor in his own household.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ πατρίδι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τοῖς συγγενεῦσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: So He could not perform any miracles there, except to lay His hands on a few of the sick and heal them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in His hometown.
The people there did not believe in Him.
Jesus could not perform any miracles there.
He only healed a few sick people.
He healed them by laying His hands on them.
passages.original: καὶ οὐκ ἐδύνατο ἐκεῖ ποιῆσαι οὐδεμίαν δύναμιν εἰ μὴ ὀλίγοις ἀρρώστοις ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας ἐθεράπευσεν

passages.text: And He was amazed at their unbelief. And He went around from village to village, teaching the people.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw the people’s unbelief.
He was amazed at their lack of faith.
Jesus traveled to the surrounding villages.
He taught the people in each village.
passages.original: καὶ ἐθαύμαζεν διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν Καὶ περιῆγεν τὰς κώμας κύκλῳ διδάσκων

passages.text: Then Jesus called the Twelve to Him and began to send them out two by two, giving them authority over unclean spirits.
passages.sermon: Jesus called the Twelve disciples to Himself.\r\nJesus began to send the Twelve disciples out in pairs.\r\nJesus gave the Twelve disciples authority over unclean spirits.
passages.original: Καὶ προσκαλεῖται τοὺς δώδεκα καὶ ἤρξατο αὐτοὺς ἀποστέλλειν δύο δύο καὶ ἐδίδου αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν ἀκαθάρτων

passages.text: He instructed them to take nothing but a staff for the journey—no bread, no bag, no money in their belts— and to wear sandals, but not a second tunic.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Twelve disciples.
He gave them instructions for their journey.
He told them to take nothing except a staff.
He told them not to take bread.
He told them not to take a bag.
He told them not to take money in their belts.
He told them to wear sandals.
He told them not to wear a second tunic.
passages.original: καὶ παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδὲν αἴρωσιν εἰς ὁδὸν εἰ μὴ ῥάβδον μόνον μὴ ἄρτον μὴ πήραν μὴ εἰς τὴν ζώνην χαλκόν ἀλλὰ ὑποδεδεμένους σανδάλια καὶ μὴ ἐνδύσησθε δύο χιτῶνας

passages.text: And He told them, “When you enter a house, stay there until you leave that area.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Twelve disciples.
He gave them instructions.
He said, “When you enter a house, stay in that house.
Remain there until you leave that place.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ὅπου ἐὰν εἰσέλθητε εἰς οἰκίαν ἐκεῖ μένετε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε ἐκεῖθεν

passages.text: If anyone will not welcome you or listen to you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that place, as a testimony against them.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He gave them instructions for their journey.
He said, “If anyone does not welcome you, leave that place.
If anyone does not listen to you, leave that place.
When you leave, shake the dust off your feet.
This act will be a testimony against those people.”
passages.original: καὶ ὃς ἂν τόπος μὴ δέξηται ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσωσιν ὑμῶν ἐκπορευόμενοι ἐκεῖθεν ἐκτινάξατε τὸν χοῦν τὸν ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς

passages.text: So they set out and preached that the people should repent.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sent out His disciples.
The disciples left.
They preached to the people.
They told the people to repent.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξελθόντες ἐκήρυξαν ἵνα μετανοῶσιν

passages.text: They also drove out many demons and healed many of the sick, anointing them with oil.
passages.sermon:
The disciples followed Jesus.
They drove out many demons.
They healed many sick people.
They anointed the sick with oil.
passages.original: καὶ δαιμόνια πολλὰ ἐξέβαλλον καὶ ἤλειφον ἐλαίῳ πολλοὺς ἀρρώστους καὶ ἐθεράπευον

passages.text: Now King Herod heard about this, for Jesus’ name had become well known, and people were saying, “John the Baptist has risen from the dead! That is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”
passages.sermon:
King Herod was the ruler.
King Herod heard about Jesus.
People knew the name of Jesus.
The name of Jesus became well known.
People spoke about Jesus.
Some people said, “John the Baptist has risen from the dead.”
They said, “That is why miraculous powers work in him.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἤκουσεν ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἡρῴδης φανερὸν γὰρ ἐγένετο τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἰωάννης ὁ Βαπτίζων ἐγήγερται ἐκ νεκρῶν καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἐνεργοῦσιν αἱ δυνάμεις ἐν αὐτῷ

passages.text: Others were saying, “He is Elijah,” and still others, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets of old.”
passages.sermon:
Some people spoke about Jesus.
They said, “He is Elijah.”
Other people spoke about Jesus.
They said, “He is a prophet.”
They said, “He is like one of the prophets from long ago.”
passages.original: ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἠλίας ἐστίν ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον ὅτι Προφήτης ὡς εἷς τῶν προφητῶν

passages.text: But when Herod heard this, he said, “John, whom I beheaded, has risen from the dead!”
passages.sermon:
King Herod heard people talking about Jesus.
Herod had ordered John the Baptist to be killed.
Herod had John beheaded.
Herod said, "John, whom I beheaded, has risen from the dead."
Herod believed John had come back to life.
passages.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἔλεγεν Ὃν ἐγὼ ἀπεκεφάλισα Ἰωάννην οὗτος ἠγέρθη

passages.text: For Herod himself had ordered that John be arrested and bound and imprisoned, on account of his brother Philip’s wife Herodias, whom Herod had married.
passages.sermon:
Herod was a ruler.
Herod gave an order.
Herod ordered his men to arrest John.
They seized John.
They tied John up.
They put John in prison.
Herod did this because of Herodias.
Herodias was the wife of Philip.
Philip was Herod’s brother.
Herod had married Herodias.
passages.original: Αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἀποστείλας ἐκράτησεν τὸν Ἰωάννην καὶ ἔδησεν αὐτὸν ἐν φυλακῇ διὰ Ἡρῳδιάδα τὴν γυναῖκα Φιλίππου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ ὅτι αὐτὴν ἐγάμησεν

passages.text: For John had been telling Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife!”
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
John was righteous.
John was holy.
John spoke to Herod.
John said to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”
John told Herod this many times.
passages.original: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὁ Ἰωάννης τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ ὅτι Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου

passages.text: So Herodias held a grudge against John and wanted to kill him. But she had been unable, because Herod feared John and protected him, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man. When he heard John’s words, he was greatly perplexed; yet he listened to him gladly.
passages.sermon:
Herodias hated John.
Herodias wanted to kill John.
Herodias could not kill John.
Herod was the ruler.
Herod feared John.
Herod knew John was a righteous man.
Herod knew John was a holy man.
Herod protected John.
Herod listened to John often.
Herod was confused by John’s words.
Herod enjoyed listening to John.
passages.original: Ἡ δὲ Ἡρῳδιὰς ἐνεῖχεν αὐτῷ καὶ ἤθελεν αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι καὶ οὐκ ἠδύνατο ὁ γὰρ Ἡρῴδης ἐφοβεῖτο τὸν Ἰωάννην εἰδὼς αὐτὸν ἄνδρα δίκαιον καὶ ἅγιον καὶ συνετήρει αὐτόν καὶ ἀκούσας αὐτοῦ πολλὰ ἠπόρει καὶ ἡδέως αὐτοῦ ἤκουεν

passages.text: On Herod’s birthday, her opportunity arose. Herod held a banquet for his nobles and military commanders and the leading men of Galilee.
passages.sermon:
Herod was the ruler.
Herodias was his wife.
Herodias wanted to harm John the Baptist.
A special day arrived.
This day was Herod’s birthday.
Herod saw an opportunity on this day.
Herod invited important people to a banquet.
He invited his nobles.
He invited his military commanders.
He invited the leading men of Galilee.
Herod held a great feast for them.
passages.original: Καὶ γενομένης ἡμέρας εὐκαίρου ὅτε Ἡρῴδης τοῖς γενεσίοις αὐτοῦ δεῖπνον ἐποίησεν τοῖς μεγιστᾶσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῖς χιλιάρχοις καὶ τοῖς πρώτοις τῆς Γαλιλαίας

passages.text: When the daughter of Herodias came and danced, she pleased Herod and his guests, and the king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you wish, and I will give it to you.”
passages.sermon:
Herod was the king.
Herodias was his wife.
Herodias had a daughter.
Herod held a banquet.
Herod invited his nobles, military commanders, and the leading men of Galilee.
Herodias’s daughter entered the banquet.
She danced before everyone.
Herod liked her dance.
His guests also liked her dance.
The king spoke to the girl.
He said, “Ask me for whatever you wish.”
He said, “I will give it to you.”
passages.original: καὶ εἰσελθούσης τῆς θυγατρὸς αὐτῆς τῆς Ἡρῳδιάδος καὶ ὀρχησαμένης ἤρεσεν τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ καὶ τοῖς συνανακειμένοις ὁ δὲ βασιλεὺς εἶπεν τῷ κορασίῳ Αἴτησόν με ὃ ἐὰν θέλῃς καὶ δώσω σοι

passages.text: And he swore to her, “Whatever you ask of me, I will give you, up to half my kingdom!”
passages.sermon:
Herod was the king.
Herod spoke to the girl.
Herod made a strong promise to her.
He said, “Whatever you ask of me, I will give you.”
He said, “I will give you up to half of my kingdom.”
passages.original: καὶ ὤμοσεν αὐτῇ Πολλά Ὅ¦τι ἐάν με αἰτήσῃς δώσω σοι ἕως ἡμίσους τῆς βασιλείας μου

passages.text: Then she went out and asked her mother, “What should I request?” And her mother answered, “The head of John the Baptist.”
passages.sermon:
The daughter of Herodias left the room.
She spoke to her mother.
She asked her mother, “What should I ask for?”
Her mother replied.
Her mother said, “Ask for the head of John the Baptist.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξελθοῦσα εἶπεν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς Τί αἰτήσωμαι Ἡ δὲ εἶπεν Τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ Βαπτίζοντος

passages.text: At once the girl hurried back to the king with her request: “I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter immediately.”
passages.sermon:
A girl went quickly to the king.
She hurried because she had a request.
She spoke to the king.
She said, “I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist.”
She asked for the head to be given on a platter.
She wanted it immediately.
passages.original: Καὶ εἰσελθοῦσα εὐθὺς μετὰ σπουδῆς πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα ᾐτήσατο λέγουσα Θέλω ἵνα ἐξαυτῆς δῷς μοι ἐπὶ πίνακι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ Βαπτιστοῦ

passages.text: The king was consumed with sorrow, but because of his oaths and his guests, he did not want to refuse her.
passages.sermon:
The king felt deep sorrow.
He had made oaths.
He had guests present.
Because of his oaths and his guests, he did not want to refuse her request.
passages.original: Καὶ περίλυπος γενόμενος ὁ βασιλεὺς διὰ τοὺς ὅρκους καὶ τοὺς ἀνακειμένους οὐκ ἠθέλησεν ἀθετῆσαι αὐτήν

passages.text: So without delay, the king commanded that John’s head be brought in. He sent an executioner, who went and beheaded him in the prison.
passages.sermon:
The king acted immediately.
He gave an order.
He told an executioner to bring John the Baptist’s head.
The king sent the executioner to the prison.
The executioner went to John in the prison.
The executioner beheaded John in the prison.
passages.original: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀποστείλας ὁ βασιλεὺς σπεκουλάτορα ἐπέταξεν ἐνέγκαι τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἀπεκεφάλισεν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ

passages.text: The man brought John’s head on a platter and presented it to the girl, who gave it to her mother.
passages.sermon:
A man brought John’s head.
He placed it on a platter.
He gave the head to the girl.
The girl gave the head to her mother.
passages.original: καὶ ἤνεγκεν τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πίνακι καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν τῷ κορασίῳ καὶ τὸ κοράσιον ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς

passages.text: When John’s disciples heard about this, they came and took his body and placed it in a tomb.
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
John’s disciples followed him.
John’s disciples heard that John had died.
They came to the place where John’s body was.
They took John’s body.
They placed John’s body in a tomb.
passages.original: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἦλθον καὶ ἦραν τὸ πτῶμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔθηκαν αὐτὸ ἐν μνημείῳ

passages.text: Meanwhile, the apostles gathered around Jesus and brought Him news of all they had done and taught.
passages.sermon:
The apostles were followers of Jesus.
The apostles gathered around Jesus.
They told Jesus everything they had done.
They told Jesus everything they had taught.
passages.original: Καὶ συνάγονται οἱ ἀπόστολοι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν αὐτῷ πάντα ὅσα ἐποίησαν καὶ ὅσα ἐδίδαξαν

passages.text: And He said to them, “Come with Me privately to a solitary place, and let us rest for a while.” For many people were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His apostles.
He said, “Come with Me by yourselves.
Let us go to a quiet place.
Let us rest for a while.”
Many people were coming and going.
The apostles did not even have time to eat.
passages.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Δεῦτε ὑμεῖς αὐτοὶ κατ’ ἰδίαν εἰς ἔρημον τόπον καὶ ἀναπαύσασθε ὀλίγον ἦσαν γὰρ οἱ ἐρχόμενοι καὶ οἱ ὑπάγοντες πολλοί καὶ οὐδὲ φαγεῖν εὐκαίρουν

passages.text: So they went away in a boat by themselves to a solitary place.
passages.sermon:
The apostles and Jesus left together.
They went by themselves.
They traveled in a boat.
They went to a solitary place.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπῆλθον ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ εἰς ἔρημον τόπον κατ’ ἰδίαν

passages.text: But many people saw them leaving and recognized them. They ran together on foot from all the towns and arrived before them.
passages.sermon:
Many people saw Jesus and His disciples leaving.
These people recognized Jesus and His disciples.
People from all the towns ran together on foot to the place where Jesus was going.
They arrived at the place before Jesus and His disciples.
passages.original: καὶ εἶδον αὐτοὺς ὑπάγοντας καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν πολλοί καὶ πεζῇ ἀπὸ πασῶν τῶν πόλεων συνέδραμον ἐκεῖ καὶ προῆλθον αὐτούς

passages.text: When Jesus stepped ashore and saw a large crowd, He had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And He began to teach them many things.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stepped ashore.
He saw a large crowd.
Jesus felt compassion for the people.
The people were like sheep without a shepherd.
Jesus began to teach the people many things.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν εἶδεν πολὺν ὄχλον καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ὅτι ἦσαν ὡς πρόβατα μὴ ἔχοντα ποιμένα καὶ ἤρξατο διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς πολλά

passages.text: By now the hour was already late. So the disciples came to Jesus and said, “This is a desolate place, and the hour is already late.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His disciples in a remote place.
The day had become very late.
The disciples came to Jesus.
They said, “This place is deserted.”
They said, “The hour is already late.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἤδη ὥρας πολλῆς γενομένης προσελθόντες αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἔρημός ἐστιν ὁ τόπος καὶ ἤδη ὥρα πολλή

passages.text: Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat.”
passages.sermon:
The disciples spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Dismiss the crowd.”
They wanted Jesus to send the people away.
They said, “Let them go to the surrounding countryside and villages.”
They wanted the people to buy food for themselves.
They said, “Let them buy something to eat.”
passages.original: ἀπόλυσον αὐτούς ἵνα ἀπελθόντες εἰς τοὺς κύκλῳ ἀγροὺς καὶ κώμας ἀγοράσωσιν ἑαυτοῖς τί φάγωσιν

passages.text: But Jesus told them, “You give them something to eat.” They asked Him, “Should we go out and spend two hundred denarii to give all of them bread to eat?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “You give them something to eat.”
The disciples replied to Jesus.
They said, “Should we go and buy bread with two hundred denarii?”
They asked, “Should we give bread to all these people to eat?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Δότε αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν Καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ἀπελθόντες ἀγοράσωμεν δηναρίων διακοσίων ἄρτους καὶ δώσομεν αὐτοῖς φαγεῖν

passages.text: “Go and see how many loaves you have,” He told them. And after checking, they said, “Five—and two fish.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Go and see how many loaves you have.”
The disciples went to check.
They returned to Jesus.
They said, “We have five loaves.”
They also said, “We have two fish.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς Πόσους ἔχετε ἄρτους ὑπάγετε ἴδετε Καὶ γνόντες λέγουσιν Πέντε καὶ δύο ἰχθύας

passages.text: Then Jesus directed them to have the people sit in groups on the green grass.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus gave them instructions.
He told them to have all the people sit down.
He told them to arrange the people in groups.
He told them to seat the people on the green grass.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπέταξεν αὐτοῖς ἀνακλῖναι πάντας συμπόσια συμπόσια ἐπὶ τῷ χλωρῷ χόρτῳ

passages.text: So they sat down in groups of hundreds and fifties.
passages.sermon: The people sat down on the grass.\r\nThey formed groups.\r\nEach group had one hundred people or fifty people.
passages.original: καὶ ἀνέπεσαν πρασιαὶ πρασιαὶ κατὰ ἑκατὸν καὶ κατὰ πεντήκοντα

passages.text: Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, Jesus spoke a blessing and broke the loaves. Then He gave them to His disciples to set before the people. And He divided the two fish among them all.
passages.sermon:
Jesus took five loaves of bread.
He also took two fish.
Jesus looked up to heaven.
He spoke a blessing.
Jesus broke the loaves of bread.
He gave the pieces to His disciples.
The disciples set the bread before the people.
Jesus divided the two fish among everyone.
passages.original: Καὶ λαβὼν τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν καὶ κατέκλασεν τοὺς ἄρτους καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα παρατιθῶσιν αὐτοῖς καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἐμέρισεν πᾶσιν

passages.text: They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces of bread and fish.
passages.sermon:
Jesus fed a large crowd with five loaves and two fish.
Everyone ate.
Everyone was satisfied.
The disciples collected the leftovers.
They filled twelve baskets with broken pieces of bread and fish.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν καὶ ἦραν κλάσματα δώδεκα κοφίνων πληρώματα καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἰχθύων

passages.text: And there were five thousand men who had eaten the loaves.
passages.sermon: Jesus fed a large crowd.\r\nFive thousand men ate the loaves.\r\nThese men were the ones who ate the bread Jesus provided.
passages.original: καὶ ἦσαν οἱ φαγόντες τοὺς ἄρτους πεντακισχίλιοι ἄνδρες

passages.text: Immediately Jesus made His disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to Bethsaida, while He dismissed the crowd.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His disciples and a large crowd.
Jesus acted immediately.
Jesus told His disciples to get into the boat.
Jesus told them to go ahead of Him to Bethsaida.
Jesus stayed behind.
Jesus dismissed the crowd.
passages.original: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἠνάγκασεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἐμβῆναι εἰς τὸ πλοῖον καὶ προάγειν εἰς τὸ πέραν πρὸς Βηθσαϊδάν ἕως αὐτὸς ἀπολύει τὸν ὄχλον

passages.text: After bidding them farewell, He went up on the mountain to pray.
passages.sermon:
Jesus said goodbye to the people.
He left them.
He went up on the mountain.
He went there to pray.
passages.original: καὶ ἀποταξάμενος αὐτοῖς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι

passages.text: When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and Jesus was alone on land.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Evening came.
The disciples’ boat was in the middle of the sea.
Jesus was alone on the land.
passages.original: Καὶ ὀψίας γενομένης ἦν τὸ πλοῖον ἐν μέσῳ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ αὐτὸς μόνος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

passages.text: He could see that the disciples were straining to row, because the wind was against them. About the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea. He intended to pass by them, but when they saw Him walking on the sea, they cried out, thinking He was a ghost— for they all saw Him and were terrified. But Jesus spoke up at once: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw the disciples.
The disciples were straining to row the boat.
The wind was against the disciples.
It was about the fourth watch of the night.
Jesus went out to the disciples.
Jesus walked on the sea.
Jesus intended to pass by the disciples.
The disciples saw Jesus walking on the sea.
The disciples thought Jesus was a ghost.
The disciples cried out.
All the disciples saw Jesus.
All the disciples were terrified.
Jesus spoke to the disciples at once.
Jesus said, “Take courage!”
Jesus said, “It is I.”
Jesus said, “Do not be afraid.”
passages.original: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτοὺς βασανιζομένους ἐν τῷ ἐλαύνειν ἦν γὰρ ὁ ἄνεμος ἐναντίος αὐτοῖς περὶ τετάρτην φυλακὴν τῆς νυκτὸς ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτοὺς περιπατῶν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἤθελεν παρελθεῖν αὐτούς οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης περιπατοῦντα ἔδοξαν ὅτι φάντασμά ἐστιν καὶ ἀνέκραξαν πάντες γὰρ αὐτὸν εἶδον καὶ ἐταράχθησαν ὁ Δὲ εὐθὺς ἐλάλησεν μετ’ αὐτῶν καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Θαρσεῖτε ἐγώ εἰμι μὴ φοβεῖσθε

passages.text: Then He climbed into the boat with them, and the wind died down. And the disciples were utterly astounded, for they had not understood about the loaves, but their hearts had been hardened.
passages.sermon:
Jesus climbed into the boat with the disciples.
The wind stopped.
The disciples were completely amazed.
They did not understand about the loaves.
Their hearts were hardened.
passages.original: καὶ ἀνέβη πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον καὶ ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος καὶ λίαν ἐκ περισσοῦ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἐξίσταντο οὐ γὰρ συνῆκαν ἐπὶ τοῖς ἄρτοις ἀλλ’ ἦν αὐτῶν ἡ καρδία πεπωρωμένη

passages.text: When they had crossed over, they landed at Gennesaret and moored the boat.
passages.sermon: Jesus and His disciples crossed the lake.\r\nThey reached the land at Gennesaret.\r\nThey moored the boat there.
passages.original: Καὶ διαπεράσαντες ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἦλθον εἰς Γεννησαρὲτ καὶ προσωρμίσθησαν

passages.text: As soon as they got out of the boat, the people recognized Jesus and ran through that whole region, carrying the sick on mats to wherever they heard He was.
passages.sermon:
Jesus got out of the boat with His disciples.
The people saw Jesus immediately.
They recognized Him at once.
The people ran throughout the whole region.
They carried the sick on mats.
They took the sick to every place where they heard Jesus was.
passages.original: καὶ ἐξελθόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου εὐθὺς ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν περιέδραμον ὅλην τὴν χώραν ἐκείνην καὶ ἤρξαντο ἐπὶ τοῖς κραβάττοις τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας περιφέρειν ὅπου ἤκουον ὅτι ἐστίν

passages.text: And wherever He went—villages and towns and countrysides—they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged Him just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak. And all who touched Him were healed.
passages.sermon:
Jesus traveled to many places.
He went into villages.
He went into towns.
He went into the countryside.
People brought sick people to the marketplaces.
They laid the sick there.
They begged Jesus to let the sick touch the edge of His cloak.
Everyone who touched Jesus was healed.
passages.original: καὶ ὅπου ἂν εἰσεπορεύετο εἰς κώμας ἢ εἰς πόλεις ἢ εἰς ἀγροὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς ἐτίθεσαν τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα κἂν τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ ἅψωνται καὶ ὅσοι ἂν ἥψαντο αὐτοῦ ἐσῴζοντο
